privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.lede: How [COMPANY NAME], trading as Kolabr, collects, uses and protects personal information when you visit our website or use the Kolabr service.
chips: Applies to kolabr.com and the Kolabr apps

nav.label: 3. Why we use it, and on what basis

short.title: In short
short.body: We collect what we need to run the service and bill for it, nothing more. We do not sell personal information, we do not use your content to train models, and content you put into a channel belongs to the organisation that put it there, not to us.

blocks.p: Kolabr is operated by [COMPANY NAME] (“we”, “us”, “our”). For personal information we collect about visitors to our website and about the people who administer and pay for a Kolabr account, we are the business that decides why and how it is used.

For content that customers put into their channels we act as a service provider, processing that information only on the customer’s instructions and only to provide the service. The customer organisation decides what goes in and why. Where the GDPR or UK GDPR applies, read “business” as controller and “service provider” as processor.

p: Our privacy contact can be reached through the
, marked for the attention of the privacy team.

blocks.p: We collect three kinds of information, and it is worth keeping them separate because we treat them differently.

The name, work email address and password of each user on your account, the organisation name, your plan, and the billing contact and payment details needed to charge you. Payment card details are handled by our payment processor and are never stored on our systems.

Everything you and your guests put into a channel: messages, files, requests and their tasks, wiki pages, scheduled events and the membership of the channel itself. We hold this on your behalf. We do not read it except where you ask us to in support, or where we are legally compelled to.

IP address, browser and device type, operating system, time zone, the pages you visit on our website, and diagnostic logs from the apps. We use this to keep the service running, investigate faults and abuse, and understand which parts of the product are used.

We do not collect special personal information, and we ask that you do not put health records, biometric data, criminal records or children’s personal information into a channel unless your own lawful basis for doing so is in place.

sections.title: Why we use it, and on what basis

head: Purpose
Information used
Lawful basis
rows: Performance of the contract with you
Account information, technical logs, channel content where you share it
Legitimate interest in protecting the service
Legitimate interest in improving the product

blocks.p: We do not use channel content to train machine-learning models, and we do not sell, rent or trade personal information to anybody.

Guests are free on every Kolabr plan, which means channels routinely contain people who are not employees of the customer: clients, contractors, parents, suppliers, funders. Two things follow from that.

ul: The customer organisation that created the channel decides who is invited and what they can see. If you are a guest and want your information removed, ask the organisation that invited you first, because they control the channel.
A guest sees only the channels they have been added to. They do not see the customer’s other channels, other clients, member lists outside those channels, or billing information.

blocks.p: If a guest contacts us directly about their information we will respond, but in most cases we will need to refer the request to the customer organisation, and we will tell you when we do.
We share personal information with a small number of service providers who help us run Kolabr, each bound by contract to process it only on our instructions:

head: Provider
What they do
Where
rows: Runs the service and holds your data
Delivers service notices and notifications by email
Website analytics, only after you accept the cookie banner

blocks.p: We update this list when it changes. We will also disclose information where we are legally required to, and we will tell the customer unless we are prohibited from doing so.

Your data is stored with cloud providers whose facilities are located in [DATA REGION]. Where we transfer personal information out of the EEA or the UK for customers there, we rely on standard contractual clauses or an adequacy decision.
You can ask where your data is held before signing up, and we will tell you plainly what is possible.

head: Information
Retention
rows: For as long as the account is active, then per the deletion rules in section 8
Held read-only for the period the customer sets, which may extend past the project
For the life of the account
Seven years after the transaction, for tax and accounting purposes
Two years after the enquiry is closed

blocks.p: Customers on paid plans can set their own retention rules for channel content. Where your rule is shorter than ours, yours applies to your content.

You can export your channel content at any time while your account is active. When an account is closed we keep the content for thirty days so it can be recovered if the closure was a mistake, then delete it from live systems. Backups holding that content are overwritten on a rolling ninety-day cycle.
A customer can ask us to delete content immediately rather than waiting out the thirty days, and we will do so in writing. Deletion is not reversible and we will say so before acting.

Depending on where you live, state privacy laws such as the California Consumer Privacy Act give you the rights below. We extend them to everyone rather than checking your address first, and where the GDPR or UK GDPR applies to you, you have these rights under that law too.

ul: Ask what personal information we hold about you and get a copy of it.
Have information that is inaccurate corrected, or information we no longer have grounds to keep deleted.
Opt out of the sale or sharing of your personal information. We do not sell or share it, and never have, so there is nothing to opt out of.
Limit how we use sensitive personal information. We do not collect any.
Object to processing we carry out on the basis of legitimate interest, and withdraw consent to marketing at any time.
Receive your information in a portable format.
Be treated no differently for exercising any of these rights.
Complain to your state attorney general, to the California Privacy Protection Agency if you are in California, or to your local supervisory authority elsewhere.

blocks.p: To exercise any of these, use the contact form. We will respond within forty-five days, and will tell you if we need longer. We may need to verify who you are first, and if you are a guest in someone else’s channel we may need to route the request through that organisation. You can name an authorised agent to make a request for you.

Data is encrypted in transit and at rest. Access to production systems is limited to the people who need it, logged, and protected by multi-factor authentication. We keep audit logs of administrative actions inside customer accounts, which customers can inspect.

No system is perfectly secure. If a breach affects your personal information we will notify you without unreasonable delay, and any regulator we are required to notify under the law of your state, with what we know, what we are doing about it, and what you should do.

Kolabr is a business product, is not directed at children, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from anyone under 13. Where a school or similar organisation uses Kolabr, channels are for staff, parents, coaches and suppliers, not for pupils. A customer must not create accounts for children under 13 or put pupil records into a channel. If you believe a child has given us personal information, contact us and we will delete it. Schools subject to FERPA or to state student-privacy laws should speak to us before using the service for anything touching student records.

We will update this policy when the service or the law changes. The date at the top always reflects the current version. Where a change materially affects how we handle your information we will tell account administrators by email at least thirty days before it takes effect, and continued use after that date means you accept the updated policy.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.lede: The agreement between you and [COMPANY NAME], trading as Kolabr, covering what we provide, what you pay, and what each of us is responsible for.
chips: Applies to kolabr.com and the Kolabr apps

short.title: In short
short.body: You own your content and can take it with you. We charge per user on your own team and never for guests. Either side can end the agreement; if we end it without cause we refund the unused portion.

blocks.p: These terms form a binding agreement between [COMPANY NAME] (“Kolabr”, “we”) and the organisation or person that opens an account (“you”, “the customer”). By creating an account, using the service or paying an invoice you accept them. If you are accepting on behalf of an organisation, you confirm you are authorised to bind it.
Where we have signed a separate written agreement with you, that agreement prevails over these terms to the extent of any conflict.

Kolabr is a collaboration service organised around channels. A channel holds conversation, requests and their tasks, scheduled events, a wiki and a membership that can include people outside your organisation.

We provide the service on a subscription basis and will make reasonable efforts to keep improving it. Features may be added, changed or withdrawn. Where we withdraw something material to how you use the product we will give at least sixty days’ notice, and you may cancel and take a pro-rata refund if the change does not work for you.
Tasks in Kolabr exist inside a request and end with it. Kolabr is not a general project-planning or task-management tool and we do not represent it as one.
Each person using Kolabr on your team needs their own account. Sharing login credentials between people is not permitted and is grounds for suspension.
Plans are priced per user on your own team. Guests, meaning people outside your organisation whom you invite into a channel, are never charged for on any plan.

Free accounts have one channel and one user, with up to thirty guests in it. Pro and Business accounts have no limit on channels or on guests: you are billed for the users on your team. A user owns work, creates channels and administers the account. A guest takes part in the channels you add them to and is never billed.
You are responsible for what happens under your account, for keeping credentials secure, and for the conduct of the guests you invite.
Subscriptions are billed monthly or annually in advance, in US dollars unless we have agreed otherwise in writing. Prices exclude sales tax, which we add where we are required to collect it.

Subscriptions renew automatically at the end of each billing period, monthly or annually, at the then-current price, until you cancel. You can cancel at any time from the account settings, and cancelling stops the next renewal rather than ending the period you have paid for. We send a reminder before an annual plan renews.

Payment is due on the invoice date. If payment fails we will retry and notify you. Accounts more than fourteen days in arrears may be suspended, and accounts more than sixty days in arrears may be closed with the data handling described in section 10.
You can change plan at any time. Upgrades take effect immediately and are charged pro-rata. Downgrades take effect at the start of the next billing period, and you keep the higher plan until then.

We may change prices with sixty days’ notice. A price change never applies to a billing period you have already paid for. If you do not accept a price change you may cancel before it takes effect and we will refund the unused portion of any period already paid.

New accounts can stay on the Free plan for as long as they like. A seven day trial of Pro or Business, with every option included and no payment card required, is available once per account. We will not charge you at the end of a trial. If you do not choose a plan the account returns to Free, and nothing is deleted.

Everything you and your guests put into Kolabr remains yours. We claim no ownership over it. You grant us only the licence we need to host, transmit, back up and display it in order to run the service for you.

p: You are responsible for having the right to put content into Kolabr, for the lawfulness of what you upload, and for the personal information of the people you invite. Our handling of that information is set out in the

blocks.p: You can export your content at any time while the account is active.
You may not use Kolabr to:

ul: Break the law, or help anyone else to.
Send unsolicited bulk messages, or use channels to distribute malware or phishing content.
Upload content you do not have the right to share, or that infringes someone else’s intellectual property.
Harass, threaten or abuse other users, including guests.
Attempt to access another customer’s data, probe or test the security of the service without our written permission, or interfere with its operation.
Resell or white-label the service without a written agreement with us.

blocks.p: We may suspend access without notice where there is a serious or ongoing breach, a security risk, or a legal obligation to act. We will tell you why as soon as we reasonably can.
We aim for 99.5% monthly availability, excluding scheduled maintenance, which we announce in advance and run outside peak hours for the majority of our customers wherever possible.
Support is provided through the contact form and through your channels. We do not guarantee a response time, though Pro and Business accounts are answered first.
The service is otherwise provided as is. We do not warrant that it will be uninterrupted, error-free, or fit for a particular purpose beyond what is described on this website.
Nothing in these terms excludes liability for fraud, for death or personal injury caused by negligence, or for anything else that cannot lawfully be excluded.

Subject to that, neither side is liable for indirect or consequential loss, loss of profit, loss of business, or loss of anticipated savings. Our total liability in any twelve-month period is limited to the fees you paid us in that period.

You remain responsible for keeping your own records where your profession or regulator requires it. Kolabr keeps a durable record of what happened in a channel, but it is not a substitute for your statutory obligations.

p: You can cancel at any time from your account settings. Cancellation takes effect at the end of the current billing period and we do not refund the remainder of a period you chose to leave early, except where section 5 or the

blocks.p: We can end the agreement on sixty days’ notice, in which case we refund the unused portion of anything you have paid. We can end it immediately for serious breach of section 7 or for non-payment beyond sixty days.
When an account closes, content is available for export for thirty days, then deleted from live systems and cycled out of backups within ninety days.

This agreement is governed by the laws of the State of [STATE NAME], without regard to its conflict of laws rules, and the state and federal courts located in [COUNTY OR CITY], [STATE NAME] have exclusive jurisdiction. Before starting proceedings, both sides agree to raise the issue in writing and give the other thirty days to resolve it.
If any provision is found unenforceable, the rest continues to apply.

We will update these terms as the service changes. Material changes are notified to account administrators by email at least thirty days before they take effect. If you do not accept a change, you may cancel before it applies and we will refund the unused portion of any period already paid.

cookies.title: Cookie policy
cookies.lede: What [COMPANY NAME], trading as Kolabr, stores on your device, why, and how to control it.
chips: Applies to kolabr.com and the Kolabr apps

short.title: In short
short.body: We use the cookies needed to log you in and keep the service secure, plus a small amount of privacy-respecting analytics. No advertising cookies, no third-party trackers, and nothing that follows you around other websites.

blocks.p: Cookies are small text files a website stores on your device so it can recognise you on your next request. Related technologies do much the same job: local storage keeps settings in your browser, and session storage forgets them when you close the tab. We use all three, and refer to them together as cookies here.
These make the service work. They cannot be switched off without breaking sign-in, and they do not require consent.

head: Purpose
What it does
Lifetime
rows: Keeps you signed in as you move between pages
Session, or 30 days if you choose to stay signed in
Confirms your identity on each request
Routes your request to a working server
Remembers light or dark mode, language and which channel you had open

blocks.p: We use privacy-respecting analytics to understand which pages are read and where people get stuck. It is aggregated, it does not build a profile of you, and it is not shared with advertisers.

head: Purpose
What it does
Lifetime
rows: Counts visits and pages viewed, in aggregate
Records faults so we can fix them

blocks.p: No advertising cookies. No retargeting pixels. No social media trackers. No cross-site tracking, and no selling of behavioural data to anyone.

A small number of providers set cookies when their functionality is used: our payment processor during checkout, and our analytics and error-monitoring providers. Each is contractually limited to processing data on our instructions, and none of them is permitted to use it for advertising.
Video calls started from a channel may set a cookie for the duration of the call to hold media settings. It expires when the call ends.
When you first visit our website you can accept or decline analytics cookies. You can change that choice at any time from the link in the website footer, and declining does not degrade the service.
Your browser also lets you block or delete cookies:

ul: Chrome: Settings, then Privacy and security, then Third-party cookies.
Safari: Settings, then Privacy.
Firefox: Settings, then Privacy and Security.
Edge: Settings, then Cookies and site permissions.

blocks.p: Blocking strictly necessary cookies will stop you being able to sign in, because there is no other way for the service to know who you are between one request and the next.

The iOS and Android apps do not use browser cookies. They store an authentication token and your preferences in the device’s secure storage, and clear both when you sign out or remove the app. They contain no advertising identifiers.
If we add or remove a cookie we will update the tables above and the date at the top of this page. Where a new cookie requires consent we will ask for it before setting it.

refunds.title: Refund policy
refunds.lede: When [COMPANY NAME], trading as Kolabr, refunds a subscription, how to ask, and how long it takes.
chips: Applies to kolabr.com and the Kolabr apps

nav.label: 7. How to ask, and how long it takes

short.title: In short
short.body: Free for as long as you like before you pay anything. Thirty days after your first payment, if it is not working for you, we refund it in full. After that we refund the unused part of an annual plan on request, and we always refund our own billing mistakes.

blocks.p: Every new account starts on Free and can trial Pro or Business for seven days with no payment card. Nothing is charged at the end of a trial and nothing starts automatically. If you do nothing, the account returns to Free.
That is deliberate. We would rather you found out the product does not suit you before any money changes hands than argue about a refund afterwards.

If you pay for a plan and decide within thirty days of your first payment that Kolabr is not right for you, tell us and we will refund that payment in full. You do not need to explain why, and we will not put you through a retention conversation.
This applies once per organisation, to the first payment on the account. It covers both monthly and annual plans.

Annual plans are discounted because the commitment helps us plan. If you cancel part-way through a year we refund the unused whole months, calculated from the end of the month in which you cancel, less the discount you received for committing annually.

head: Situation
What we refund
rows: Cancel within 30 days of first payment
Cancel later in an annual term
Unused whole months, less the annual discount already taken
Nothing further; the plan runs to the end of the paid month
We end the agreement without cause
We materially withdraw a feature you rely on
A price increase you do not accept

blocks.p: Monthly subscriptions are not refunded part-way through a month. Cancel at any time and the plan runs to the end of the period you have paid for, with no further charge after that. There is no notice period and no cancellation fee.

Removing users or moving to a lower plan takes effect at the start of the next billing period rather than immediately, and we do not refund the difference for the current period. You keep the higher plan and the seats until the period ends.
Adding users mid-period is charged pro-rata, so you only pay for the part of the period they are actually on the account.

If we charge you the wrong amount, charge you after you cancelled, or bill you for guests, that is our mistake and we refund it in full as soon as we confirm it. Tell us through the contact form with the invoice number and we will deal with it without argument.
Guests are never billable on any plan. If a guest ever appears on an invoice, it is an error.

sections.title: How to ask, and how long it takes

p: , or raise it in your channel if you are already a customer, with the invoice number and what happened.

blocks.p: We confirm within two business days. Approved refunds are returned to the original payment method within ten business days, subject to your bank’s own timing, which we do not control.

Refunds are made in the currency you were charged in. Where a currency conversion or bank fee was applied by your provider, the amount you receive may differ slightly, and we cannot recover those fees.

Nothing here limits any right you have under the law of your state, including any right to cancel an automatically renewing subscription. Where this policy gives you more than the law requires, this policy applies.

dpa.title: Data processing addendum
dpa.lede: The terms on which [COMPANY NAME], trading as Kolabr, processes personal information that a customer puts into its channels. This addendum forms part of the agreement and applies whenever the customer is the controller and Kolabr is the processor.
chips: Forms part of the Kolabr terms of service

short.title: In short
short.body: What your people and your clients write in a channel is yours. We process it only to run the service, only on your instructions, and we do not use it to train anything or sell it to anyone. If you need a signed copy for procurement, ask and we will send one.

blocks.p: This addendum applies to personal information contained in customer content: everything your team and the people you invite put into a channel. For that information you are the controller, or the business, and we are the processor, or the service provider.
For information we collect about you directly, such as the person who administers the account, who pays and who contacts support, we are the controller and our privacy policy applies instead.

head: What it covers
rows: Providing the Kolabr service: channels, chat, requests, meetings, scheduled events and the wiki
For as long as the account is active, then as set out in section 9
Your staff, and the clients, partners, suppliers and other guests you invite into channels
Names, email addresses, profile images, message and file content, request records and activity logs
None is required by the service. You should not put it into a channel without agreeing that with us first

blocks.p: We process customer content only on your documented instructions, which are the agreement, this addendum and your use of the product's own settings. If we believe an instruction breaks data protection law, we will tell you rather than carry it out.
We do not use customer content to train machine learning models, to build profiles, or for any purpose of our own. We do not sell it or share it for advertising.
Everyone at Kolabr who can reach customer content is bound by confidentiality obligations that survive the end of their engagement, and access is limited to the people who need it to do their job.

We keep appropriate technical and organisational measures, described in the security section of our privacy policy: encryption in transit and at rest, multi-factor authentication on production access, least-privilege access, and audit logging of administrative actions inside customer accounts.
Customers on Business can enforce single sign-on, set their own retention rules and export the audit log.

p: You give general authorisation for us to engage sub-processors. The current list, with what each one does and where, is in the

blocks.p: We stay responsible for what a sub-processor does, and we impose the same obligations on them that this addendum imposes on us. We will give at least thirty days' notice before adding or replacing one, and if you reasonably object on data protection grounds you may end the affected part of the service without penalty for the unused period.

If someone exercises a data protection right and the information is in your channels, the request is yours to answer, because it is your content and you decide what happens to it. The product lets you find, export, correct and delete it yourself. Where you cannot, we will help within a reasonable time.
We will give you the information you reasonably need for a data protection impact assessment or a consultation with a regulator, so far as it relates to our processing.

If we become aware of a personal data breach affecting customer content, we will notify you without undue delay and in any event within seventy-two hours of becoming aware, with what we know, what we are doing about it and what we suggest you do. We will not notify your regulator or your people on your behalf unless you ask us to.

Customer content is held in [DATA REGION]. Where we transfer personal information out of the EEA, the UK or Switzerland, we rely on the standard contractual clauses, with the UK addendum where the UK GDPR applies, or on an adequacy decision where one covers the transfer.

You can export your content at any time while the account is active. When the agreement ends, you have thirty days to export it. After that we delete it, and it is removed from backups within a further ninety days.
We will keep information for longer only where the law requires it, and where we do, this addendum keeps applying to it.

We will give you the information you need to show that we are meeting this addendum. Where that is not enough, you may audit us once in any twelve month period, on thirty days' notice, at your cost, during business hours and without disrupting the service. A recognised third-party report, where we hold one, satisfies this.
If this addendum conflicts with the agreement, this addendum wins for anything to do with the processing of personal information. Everything else in the agreement continues to apply.
If you need a signed copy, or your own paper, ask through the contact form and we will work with you.
